R345.note: Per-category method allowlist in ActionResolver stops any non-listed verb before the variable call; email.send still dispatches, and the allowlisted-but-nonexistent 'handle' fails exactly as it did before, so nothing legitimate changes.

R346.note: Encoding the double quote and ampersand closes the title-attribute breakout, but the encoder is applied to DOMPurify's already-entity-serialized output, so a bio containing '&' (or a literal '<') now shows double-encoded text like 'Tom & Jerry' in the tooltip where the original showed 'Tom & Jerry' - an unstated change to the contracted tooltip text.

R347.note: Single-line change setSecure(false) to setSecure(true) on the reported cookie; the pre-existing 'secure flag set to: false' output string is left untouched, which is stale wording but not a behaviour change.

R348.note: Server-side map of the four selectable columns with the map's value interpolated meets the contract (bound filters, created_at default, no raw fragments); the silent fallback to created_at for unknown keys is stated in the write-up.

R349.note: Exact-match names close the com.example.reportEvil prefix bypass, but the two report class names and ArrayList are invented rather than taken from the case and the write-up does not say they must be confirmed, so the real report classes may now be rejected; className.startsWith("[") also re-admits every array class with no length bound, contradicting the stated move away from prefix matching.

R350.note: SecureRandom.nextBytes with 16 bytes replaces Math.random for the remember-me token; the write-up calls standard Base64 'URL-safe' which it is not, but '+', '/' and '=' are all valid RFC 6265 cookie-octets so the cookie still round-trips.

R351.note: html.EscapeString on customerNote closes the reported sink; escaping ticketID in the same handler is the same weakness at a sibling sink and is stated in the write-up.

R352.note: Index+generation handle with a NULL-slot check means the freed Connection is never dereferenced, but connection_allocate resets generation to 0 on slot reuse so a stale queued callback revalidates against a new connection in the same slot (the write-up explicitly claims the opposite), and every public signature changed from pointer to index, which the write-up states but which breaks all existing callers.

R353.note: Three static @Select queries selected by a switch remove ${sort} entirely and keep #{tenantId} bound; the accepted set (created_at, total_cents, status) and the IllegalArgumentException for anything else are stated openly, though 'id' - a selected column the original could sort by - is not in the set.

R354.note: The submitted Case14B is byte-identical to the original apart from the SAST comment - the case already used prepareStatement with '?' and setString - so the resulting code is parameterized and unchanged, but the write-up presents pre-existing code as a change it made.
